title: Eventual vanishing of affine cartesian higher-image sections
statement: Under the hypotheses of the cartesian higher-image construction, if U is an affine etale object of the limiting base and a section of the stage cartesian higher image over U maps to zero in the limit, then some later transition maps that section to zero.

source.place: Lemma 59.51.8, second proof; affine section reduction

proof.text: Apply the local affine-cover vanishing theorem to obtain a later stage and a finite etale cover on which the transitioned section restricts to zero. Apply the finite-cover separatedness argument to conclude that the transitioned section itself is zero.

proof_origin.place: Second proof, affine etale section step

lean.statement:
theorem exists_cartesianHigherImage_affine_section_eq_zero
    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] [IsCofiltered I]
    (D : I ⥤ Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [∀ i, QuasiCompact (D.obj i).hom] [∀ i, QuasiSeparated (D.obj i).hom]
    [∀ {i j : I} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map a).left]
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit ((Over.forget _).mapCone c))
    [QuasiCompact c.pt.hom] [QuasiSeparated c.pt.hom]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (q : ℕ) (U : c.pt.left.Etale) [IsAffine U.left] (i : I)
    (x : (cartesianHigherImageStage D c f F q i).obj.obj (Opposite.op U))
    (hx : (cartesianHigherImageLeg D c f F q i).hom.app (Opposite.op U) x = 0) :
    ∃ (j : I) (a : j ⟶ i),
      (cartesianHigherImageTransition D c f F q a).hom.app (Opposite.op U) x = 0
